companies.valuation_note: No credible public valuation; equity-only total shown (Tracxn's ~$519M total includes large debt facilities)
companies.employees_note: More than 10,000 employees, on Amartha's own account: its July 2025 release says "lebih dari 10.000 karyawan (A-Team)" spread across Indonesia, and chairman Rudiantara repeated the figure in August 2025, adding that about 9,000 of them are penyuluh lapangan — field officers. Those field officers are payroll, not mitra: Amartha's own Business Partner (staf lapangan) postings offer a fixed monthly wage from Rp 3.5 million, THR, a company mess and employee training, which is the same test that lets J&T's salaried couriers count and keeps Gojek's drivers out. LinkedIn sees 1,010 profiles and Tracxn 2,613 because neither instrument reaches a field officer in a village — and 10,000 minus the 9,000 field officers leaves about 1,000 office staff, which is what LinkedIn shows to within 1%. The reference class agrees: PNM Mekaar, the state-owned lender running the same weekly-group model, employs 62,184 people for 15.4 million borrowers, about one staff member per 250. Amartha has disbursed Rp 35 trillion to 3.3 million women across more than 50,000 villages; the same ratio puts it in exactly this band. The old 5,000 was the midpoint of a LinkedIn size band and measured nothing.

companies.employees_note: 217 people on the Hijra LinkedIn page, read live on 18 Oct 2026. It is the group’s current page (it links to hijra.id and gives Jakarta Selatan as headquarters); its self-declared size band, 51-200, sits just below the count. The group’s older page under the ALAMI name still lists 525 people, and that count is not used: LinkedIn keeps counting people who leave without updating their profiles, and the group cut staff in September 2023 (DailySocial) and by about 40% in February 2025 (DealStreetAsia, Tech in Asia). Two dated figures support the order of size: the bank’s own 2025 annual report gives 80 employees at Hijra Bank on 31 Dec 2025 (88 a year earlier), the bank alone, and Revelio Labs’ workforce model reads 222 for March 2026. companies.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): founded in 2018 by three former bankers, Dima Djani, Harza Sandityo and Bembi Juniar, as ALAMI, a sharia peer-to-peer financing platform, and venture-backed since 2019 (see the funding note). Its bank is a small rural bank the group bought in 2021, not an incumbent’s unit. Test 2 (own entity): the group has traded as Hijra since its rebrand of 20 Dec 2022, and the row counts the whole group, where its people, funding rounds and brand sit. ALAMI’s own ownership page names Alami Technologies Pte. Ltd., a Singapore company, as the 85% owner of PT Alami Fintek Sharia, the OJK-licensed P2P platform, with PT Alami Teknologi Sharia holding the other 15%. The bank’s 2025 annual report names PT Alami Teknologi Sharia as the 99.99% owner of PT Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Syariah Hijra Alami, the bank behind the Hijra Bank app launched on 6 Dec 2022. The bank was PT BPRS Cempaka Al Amin, licensed in 2009; it became BPRS Hijra Alami in May 2021 and took its present name under the 2023 financial-sector law (Hijra notice, 4 Sep 2023). Test 3 (headcount): see the headcount note. Geography: the group office is Plaza 89 on Jl. H.R. Rasuna Said, Setiabudi, the address on ALAMI’s site and on the group’s job listings; Hijra Bank’s own office is Ruko Plaza Pondok Indah 1 in Kebayoran Lama, also Jakarta Selatan. Liveness: Hijra Bank posted its report for the quarter to September 2026 in October 2026, ALAMI posted its 2025 financial statements on 30 Jun 2026 and shows a current repayment rate, and both LinkedIn pages carried posts in the four weeks before 18 Oct 2026. Sector: Hijra Bank is a sharia rural bank (BPRS), a narrower licence than a commercial bank (OJK’s rules bar rural banks from current accounts and foreign exchange, as Tech in Asia set out in Aug 2021), and it employed 80 of the group’s roughly 217 people at the end of 2025. The row therefore stays in Fintech, priced at the fintech output anchor, rather than in Digital Banking, which holds licensed commercial banks. Doubtful: the group-wide headcount, and how much equity the unsized rounds added. Namesakes: Hijra Bank S.C. in Ethiopia (hijra-bank.com) is an unrelated bank.
companies.funding_floor_note: the pre-seed, the equity share of the Jan 2021 Series A and the 2022 and 2023 rounds were never sized
companies.funding_note: Sized equity on record adds up to at least US$19.0 million; the figure is a floor. Counted: (1) the seed round closed in late 2019, US$1.5 million led by Golden Gate Ventures with Agaeti Ventures, RHL Ventures and the angel investor Aamir Rahim (ALAMI’s release of 13 Nov 2019 names the investors; the amount comes from the January 2021 announcement as reported by Tech in Asia and TNGlobal); (2) the Series A+, US$17.5 million of equity led by EV Growth and Quona Capital, with AC Ventures and Golden Gate Ventures following on (DealStreetAsia, 13 Aug 2021; Tech in Asia, 19 Aug 2021). Not counted, because no amount was published: the May 2019 pre-seed led by tryb Group, an equity investment according to The Business Times; the January 2021 Series A led by AC Ventures and Golden Gate Ventures with Quona Capital, announced only as more than US$20 million of equity and debt combined, with no split, so none of it can be counted as equity; the October 2022 pre-Series B led by East Ventures’ growth fund with AC Ventures, Quona Capital, FEBE Ventures and Capria Ventures (East Ventures release, 10 Oct 2022); ParagonCorp’s investment through Paragon Beneva Investama (Kontan, 20 Dec 2022); and the growth round led by Intudo Ventures with East Ventures, AC Ventures, Quona Capital and Golden Gate Ventures (ALAMI release, 5 Oct 2023; Bisnis.com reported that the amount was not disclosed). Debt is never counted: the Lendable facility of April 2022, up to US$30 million, is a financing line, not equity. This row used to show US$37.5 million, which added the whole January 2021 equity-and-debt total to the Series A+; that figure is withdrawn. In a July 2024 founder profile on BackScoop the group described its lifetime raise as around US$50 million of equity and US$50 million of debt; that total is not broken down by round, so it is not counted.

J&T Global Express (HKEX: 1519) is Cayman-incorporated and worth HK$95.1B (~US$12.2B) on 28 Aug 2026, but its FY2025 accounts report four geographic segments and none of them is Indonesia: Southeast Asia US$4.50B revenue, China US$6.71B, New Markets US$0.87B, Cross-border US$0.08B. China is the largest single segment by revenue, so the group market capitalisation is majority non-Indonesian; it was carried on this row until 29 Aug 2026 and has been taken out. The global J&T group, which moved 30.1 billion parcels in 2025, is far larger.

companies.valuation_note: INDONESIA ONLY — an estimate, not a disclosed figure. Grab Holdings is worth US$14.72B (NASDAQ: GRAB, 28 Aug 2026). Its Form 20-F reports revenue by country, and Indonesia is US$715M of US$3,370M group revenue in FY2025 — 21.2%, the third-largest of its eight markets after Malaysia and Singapore. Carving the market capitalisation at that share gives US$3,123M, published as US$3.1B (rounded down). The assumption is that a dollar of Indonesian revenue carries the same multiple as a dollar of Malaysian or Singaporean revenue; Indonesia is Grab's lower-margin market, so if anything this overstates it. At 15%–25% of group value the range is US$2.2B–3.7B. Working: scripts/est-valuation-grab.py. OVO is ~90% Grab-owned and consolidated, so its value sits inside this figure and the OVO row is held out of the combined valuation.
companies.employees_note: INDONESIAN PAYROLL ONLY, and an estimate. Grab publishes no country headcount; group full-time employees were 12,012 at 31 Dec 2025 (ESG Report 2025, GRI 2-7), of which 865 are Everrise supermarket staff in Malaysia and 22 are Infermove in China. The remaining 11,125 allocated on Indonesia's 21.2% share of group revenue gives 2,360, published as 2,350. Driver-partners and merchant-partners are NOT counted — Grab's own filings describe them as independent partners, not employees. Also excluded: 1,242 fixed-term and 3,956 temporary agency workers, which Grab reports only group-wide.

B-12 — the operating head office is used here, as on every other row. Indonesian revenue, group revenue, employee counts and the partner/employee distinction are all read off the FY2025 Form 20-F and the ESG report; the market capitalisation off stockanalysis.com on 28 Aug 2026. Other Indonesian entities named in the 20-F: PT Solusi Pengiriman Indonesia, PT Bumi Cakrawala Perkasa, PT Visionet Internasional (OVO). Grab holds under 50% of PT Super Bank Indonesia Tbk, which is not consolidated and is not in this census.

The group has lately been returning capital, not raising it: an employee-share buyback at a valuation above US$330B (Aug 2025) and a General Atlantic secondary sale at about US$550B (Feb 2026), both per Reuters. The US$1.5B the group put INTO Indonesia in January 2024 is the PT Tokopedia transaction and sits on that row, not this one.
companies.valuation_note: No Indonesian figure exists and there is no basis to carve one. ByteDance is private and its marks are group-wide — about US$550B in a Feb 2026 General Atlantic secondary sale, above US$330B in the Aug 2025 buyback, both per Reuters — and the group publishes no Indonesia revenue split, so a Grab-style carve-out (Indonesia share of revenue x group value) is impossible; anything printed here would be invented. Indonesia being TikTok’s largest market by users is a reach fact, not a valuation basis.
companies.employees_note: INDONESIAN PAYROLL ONLY, and no publishable figure exists. TikTok/ByteDance has never filed or stated an Indonesian headcount: LinkedIn has no Indonesia-scoped employer page (the global TikTok and ByteDance pages mix every market), and Indonesian job boards self-declare bands — Kitalulus’s ByteDance profile says "more than 2,000 employees" (read Feb 2026), a band this census never publishes as a count. What is on record: TikTok confirmed an Indonesian restructuring on 2 Jul 2026 without disclosing a number (CNBC Indonesia; Fortune IDN); DPR leadership put about 200 voluntary packages on the TikTok Shop–Tokopedia side while press reports ran to 1,250 — both sides are carried on the PT Tokopedia row, whose remaining staff are counted there, not here. A "2,000 staff in Indonesia" figure circulated in 2023 coverage could not be re-sourced and is withdrawn rather than reused. Creators, sellers and affiliate promoters are mitra by construction and are never counted.
companies.operating_evidence: TikTok’s own usage figures, stated by its GM of Content Operations SEA Angga Anugrah Putra at the TikTok SEA Growth Summit (Jakarta, 30 Jul 2025, Kompas): more than 160M monthly active users in Indonesia in Q1 2025 — TikTok’s largest market in Southeast Asia (Vietnam 70M, Thailand 50M; 460M across 11 SEA markets) — up from 10M MAU in Jul 2018 (SVP Zhen Liu, same Kompas piece). CEO Shou Zi Chew pledged a US$10B multi-year Indonesian investment in Jakarta, Jun 2023 (Liputan6/Bisnis). Regulatory trail: Komdigi suspended TikTok’s PSE registration (TDPSE) on 3 Oct 2025 after TikTok supplied only partial data on TikTok Live monetisation during the 25–30 Aug 2025 protests (suspected online-gambling-linked gifting), and lifted the suspension on 5 Oct 2025 once the data was delivered (Komdigi releases; ANTARA; Kompas). Through TikTok Nusantara (SG) Pte. Ltd. the group has held 75.01% of PT Tokopedia since 31 Jan 2024; KPPU fined that entity Rp 15B on 29 Sep 2025 for late merger notification (Putusan 02/KPPU-M/2025).
companies.verify_note: ByteDance’s own Indonesian operation — the TikTok APP side — counted under the global-parent rule; the e-commerce arm runs through PT Tokopedia (75.01% TikTok-held), which has its own census row, so nothing here double-counts it. ENTITY CHAIN: PT MP Games is TikTok’s Indonesian contracting entity per TikTok for Business’s own Indonesia VAT/WHT help page (last updated May 2026 — Indonesian advertisers contract with "PT MP Games or TikTok Pte. Ltd."; tax invoices arrive from mail.bytedance.net). The Ministry of Law registry (business number 291927, via companieshouse.id) has PT MP Games at Sinar Mas Land Plaza Sudirman Lt. 31; an amendment snapshot (iditrix) shows the earlier registered address at Gandaria 8 Office Tower 09D-E — TikTok Indonesia’s long-time office. The same PT holds the registered copyrights for BABE, ByteDance’s Indonesian news app — the registry-side tie to the group. The TikTok app itself is registered under TikTok Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) on Komdigi’s PSE register. ByteDance (founded 2012, Beijing) is venture-built and still private, so the built-by-tech-money test passes on the group itself. Operating as of 30 Aug 2026: tiktok.com serves; the Jul 2026 restructuring did not close the Indonesian operation.

No filing, dated company statement or 2025-2026 press figure was found, so the live count is used, but it very likely runs high. The page is the old group page: HappyFresh had about 400 employees across three countries in July 2022 (Asian Business Review, 12 Jul 2022), before it left Malaysia and Thailand that September and before its holding company was wound up in 2023, and the count has barely moved since. A company-data record of the page's members puts 87 of those with a known location in Indonesia and 34 abroad, 21 of them in Malaysia and 8 in Thailand, where HappyFresh no longer operates. The self-declared band of 51-200 may be closer to today's Indonesia-only team, but it is not a count. Personal shoppers and riders may also be on the page; their employment terms are not published. Tracker context only, not used: PitchBook shows 592 employees.
companies.funding_note: Equity raised totals at least US$97 million, a floor because the seed and Series B amounts were never published. Series A: US$12 million, announced 14 Sep 2015, led by Vertex Ventures and Sinar Mas Digital Ventures with Asia Venture Group, BEENEXT, Ardent Capital, 500 Startups and Cherry Ventures (HappyFresh's own release; TechCrunch, 16 Sep 2015). Series B: led by Samena Capital with Vertex Ventures and Sinar Mas Digital Ventures, announced 29 Aug 2016 without an amount (TechCrunch), so it is not counted; the US$12 million that TechCrunch later cited is the Series A alone, so no round is counted twice. Series C: US$20 million, announced in April 2019, led by the Mirae Asset-Naver Asia Growth Fund with Line Ventures, Singha Ventures and Grab Ventures (TechCrunch, 22 Apr 2019; The Nation, 24 Apr 2019; HappyFresh's own blog). Series D: US$65 million, announced 27 Jul 2021, led by Naver Financial and Gafina B.V. with STIC Investments, LB Investment and Mirae Asset, and returning investors Mirae Asset-Naver Asia Growth Fund and Z Venture Capital (TechCrunch, 27 Jul 2021; HappyFresh's own release, 28 Jul 2021; The Jakarta Post). Bloomberg, carried by The Business Times on 7 Sep 2022, put the total at 'at least US$97 million in equity funding in addition to debt financing'. Not counted: the money that let HappyFresh resume in Indonesia in September 2022, which was venture debt from Genesis, InnoVen and Mars (Kumparan and Katadata, 22-23 Sep 2022). Why the group figure is kept: the rounds were raised by the Singapore holding company, iCart Group Pte. Ltd. (Rajah & Tann's Series D deal note), but the group was headquartered and run from Jakarta from the start (HappyFresh's own 2015 release; Jakarta Globe, 14 Sep 2015; Bloomberg, 2022, which calls Indonesia its home market), and its Malaysian, Thai and earlier Taiwanese and Philippine businesses were arms of that Jakarta-run company; today it operates only in Indonesia. So it is counted as an Indonesian company with a Singapore holding company, not as a foreign group's Indonesian arm. That holding company has since been wound up: a provisional liquidator was appointed on 18 Jul 2023 after its director declared that it could not continue by reason of its liabilities, and on 17 Aug 2023 it resolved to wind up voluntarily (Singapore Government Gazette, 21 Jul and 23 Aug 2023; DealStreetAsia, 20 Jul 2023), with the final meeting called for 26 Sep 2025. The investors' money went into that company; the Indonesian operating company, PT iCart Group Indonesia, kept trading, and who owns it now is not public. In May-September 2026 DealStreetAsia reported that Sayurbox and HappyFresh were weighing a merger, the second report noting a link to Trikomsel; no deal has been announced.

method.method_summary: Every company is a hand-checked public-source record: legal entity, head-office address, disclosed funding, and a headcount taken from the best available source under a published ladder. Economic weight is then estimated, not reported: headcount x a sector gross-value-added-per-worker anchor derived from BPS DKI Jakarta's 2024 PDRB and 2023 Sakernas employment tables (Rp 475-1,075 million per worker by sector, Rp 675 million default), discounted so startup output is not valued at telco- and bank-average productivity. That gives direct GVA; a single portfolio-wide x1.5 multiplier gives the indirect figure, applied once and never to GMV, funding or valuation. USD is converted at Rp 17,701/US$ (29 Aug 2026). The multiplier is a judgment informed by Indonesian input-output literature on output multipliers rather than a measured GVA multiplier; single-company estimates carry at least +/-50% error and only the sums are meant to be read closely.

caveats: GVA-per-worker heterogeneity is the dominant error source: a pre-revenue startup's true GVA is roughly payroll + depreciation (can be 3-5x below the anchor), while a scaled profitable platform can sit several times above it. Single-company estimates carry at least +/-50% error; sums over many companies are far more reliable than any one row.

Global-parent rows (Grab, Shopee, Lazada, Ninja Xpress, J&T) carry Indonesia-only figures. A group market capitalisation or a parent's regional funding is never reprinted as an Indonesian number; where no Indonesian basis is disclosed the cell is a dash. Their headcounts are Indonesian payroll only, with gig partners excluded, so these companies' true economic footprint is understated by design — as it is for every marketplace and logistics row.

Headcount inputs are bands/estimates (LinkedIn etc.), often mixing contractors and interns; gig workers (drivers, couriers, sellers) are deliberately excluded, so marketplace/logistics ecosystem contribution is understated by design.

GMV is not GVA: for marketplaces only take-rate revenue net of intermediate consumption is value added. Never scale from GMV, funding, or valuation - that is the main double-counting trap. Sanity gate: direct GVA should not exceed take-rate revenue, and for pre-revenue firms should look like payroll.

Licensed banks carry their own GVA anchor (Rp 1,680 million per worker), not the fintech one. It is BPS DKI Jakarta's sector K (financial services and insurance) figure of Rp 1,976 million per worker at the same 0.85 discount used elsewhere, and it deliberately sits above the Rp 1,282 million M,N cap: that cap exists to stop STARTUPS being valued at bank-average productivity, and licensed banks are the very firms whose output produces the K average, so it does not apply to them. Pricing a bank at the fintech anchor would understate it, not inflate it. The estimate stays conservative against what these banks report — SeaBank's 776 staff come to Rp 1.3T here against Rp 8.18T of 2025 revenue and Rp 678bn of net profit.

Jakarta J/K sector averages (2.453 and 1.976 jt/worker) are dominated by telco networks and bank balance sheets; using them uncapped would overstate startup GVA 2-3x. The M,N professional-services cap (1.282 jt) is itself a judgment call, as are the 0.70-0.85 discount factors and blend weights - they are stated explicitly so they can be stress-tested.

Vintage mismatch (deliberately conservative): anchors are at 2023 current prices matched to Aug-2023 employment, applied to 2026 headcounts. Jakarta nominal PDRB rose 6.9% in 2024 alone, so true 2026 nominal GVA per worker is likely 10-20% higher than these anchors.

Sakernas counts workers by residence, PDRB by place of production; Bodetabek commuters mean the raw per-worker figures are somewhat inflated for all sectors (works against conservatism; partially offset by the cap and discounts).
Real estate (L) per-worker GVA (1.464 jt) is an artifact of imputed rents on owner-occupied dwellings and was excluded as a prop anchor.

The 1.5 indirect+induced multiplier applies to direct GVA once, portfolio-wide. Do not sum per-company indirect effects as if additive with other companies' direct GVA - one startup's indirect effect is partly another's direct GVA.
Jakarta agri (A) employment is tiny (23.7k) so its per-worker figure is noisy; the agri anchor leans on the blend, not the raw cell.
FX (17.701 IDR/USD, 29 Aug 2026) converts 2023-price IDR anchors, so USD figures mix vintages slightly; refresh FX at publication time.
Company-level nulls: where headcount is unknown, output null rather than imputing from funding or valuation.
audit_issues: Multiplier basis mismatch (non-refuting): Zuhdi (2014) reports simple OUTPUT multipliers for Indonesian ICT, not GVA multipliers; 1.5 is inside the plausible Type I/II GVA band and is applied once portfolio-wide with an anti-double-counting caveat, but the basis should be described as a judgment informed by output-multiplier literature rather than a measured GVA multiplier

Info-comm startup anchors (1000-1075 jt) are ~1.4-1.5x the economy average, below the 2-10x sanity band's lower edge - this is deliberate and documented (raw J cell 2453 jt = 3.4x average is telco-dominated; M,N cap 1282 x 0.70-0.85 discounts), so it biases conservative, not wrong; verified 1282 x 0.85 = 1090 ~ fintech 1075
Vintage mismatch is real but disclosed and conservative: 2023-price anchors applied to 2026 headcounts understate nominal GVA by an acknowledged 10-20% (Jakarta nominal PDRB grew 6.9% in 2024 alone)

All primary-source figures reproduced exactly: BRS Table 1 gives 2024 PDRB ADHB Rp 3,679.36T and J sector Rp 342.48T (9.31%); caveat cells J 2453, K 1976, M,N 1282 jt/worker all recompute to the digit from 2023 ADHB / Sakernas Aug-2023; economy average 720 jt/worker (2024) matches the ~700M sanity check; FX 17,701 verified live against open.er-api.com on 2026-08-29
method.global_parent_rule: Foreign groups' Indonesian operations are counted at their Indonesian size only. Grab, Shopee, Lazada, Ninja Xpress and J&T all run Jakarta head offices with Indonesian staff, so they belong in a Jakarta census — but a group market capitalisation, or capital a Singapore or Cayman parent raised for eight countries, is not an Indonesian figure. Value is published only where the group discloses a basis to carve an Indonesian share from (Grab's Form 20-F reports revenue by country); otherwise the cell is a dash and the note says what the group is worth and why that is a different claim. Jobs are people on an Indonesian payroll: driver-, courier-, merchant- and seller-partners are mitra, not employees, and are never counted — and a payroll that is mostly frontline (couriers, store crews, field officers) is marked as such and priced at the national frontline anchor rather than a Jakarta sector average.
method.headcount_rule: Headcount is taken from the best source available, in this order: a company filing; the company's own published statement; named reporting that attributes a figure to the company; a live LinkedIn people count; a dated vendor workforce model. LinkedIn is a floor, not a count — couriers, baristas and village field officers do not keep profiles, and people who have left stay listed for months, so the same number runs low for a labour-intensive business and high for one that has just shrunk. The midpoint of a LinkedIn size band is not a source and is never published: a row with nothing better shows a dash and contributes no jobs and no output. Jobs mean payroll — salaried field and delivery staff count, platform drivers, couriers, merchants and sellers engaged as mitra do not — and a subsidiary whose staff are already inside a counted parent's filing is not counted twice. Jobs count the company's whole Indonesian payroll, frontline included: salaried couriers, sorters, store crews, gym coaches and village field officers are employment the company creates and are counted — driver-, courier-, merchant- and seller-partners (mitra) never are. Rows whose payroll is mostly frontline carry a `frontline` mark saying what kind of workforce the number is, and where the company itself discloses the split — Amartha's ~9,000 field officers, FORE's 97% store staff — the office/frontline breakdown is published on the row. So the jobs total states the employment these companies actually carry, and the output model prices frontline payroll at the national frontline anchor rather than a Jakarta sector average.
method.frontline_rule: A frontline worker is priced at Rp 149 million of value added a year — the BPS national economy-wide average: PDB 2023 at current prices, Rp 20,892.4 trillion, over 139.85 million employed (Sakernas, August 2023) — instead of a DKI Jakarta sector anchor. A courier, barista or village field officer adds roughly what the average Indonesian worker adds, not a Jakarta digital-sector multiple. Rows marked `frontline` price their whole payroll at this anchor; rows with a company-published split price the office share at the sector anchor and the frontline share at this one. Cross-check: FORE's audited FY2025 accounts imply about Rp 124 million of true value added per worker — within 20% of this anchor on the one audited case.

scope.rule_id: Sebuah perusahaan dihitung ketika ia dibangun atau dibeli oleh uang teknologi atau modal ventura — bukan dijalankan sebagai lini produk pemain lama — ketika ia entitas hukumnya sendiri, dan ketika jumlah pekerjanya bisa ditelusuri sumbernya. Ketiganya harus terpenuhi. Geografi: seluruh Indonesia sejak 28 Sep 2026. Sensus dimulai dari Jabodetabek (29 Agu 2026), lalu cekungan Bandung (30 Agu) dan metro Sarbagita di Bali selatan (31 Agu), dan kini menghitung perusahaan di mana pun kantor pusatnya di Indonesia. Cakupan di luar tiga metro itu masih dibangun, kota demi kota.
